citation: Liu (2019). HAMS: A Frequency-Domain Preprocessor for Wave-Structure Interactions: Theory, Development, and Application. Journal of Marine Science and Engineering 7, 81.
description: HAMS is Yingyi Liu's Fortran 90 program for frequency-domain analysis of wave interactions with floating or submerged marine structures. It uses boundary integral equations within potential-flow theory and accepts triangular or quadrilateral panel meshes. Inputs are structure geometry, water depth and wave conditions; outputs include hydrodynamic coefficients, wave-excitation forces, motion response operators and free-surface elevations. Geographic application is unrestricted by a supplied site, while panel size and frequency choices define numerical resolution. Source is free under Apache-2.0, with theory references and example material. A limitation is that potential-flow assumptions do not represent all viscous or strongly nonlinear phenomena, and mesh quality affects accuracy. HAMS can prepare hydrodynamic models for offshore-energy and port simulations. OpenFOAM (model-openfoam) provides related CFD methods with different assumptions. No mesh, model archive or executable was downloaded.
